A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GA-Rollback and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. Content can be reliably matched across their reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, case studies and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct in Table 6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Appendix D retain the same rollback procedure, feedback evaluation, Wait-Info strategy and assistant prompts. Validation before irreversible actions is suggested in Limitations, without becoming an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Game of 24, ALFWorld and Webshop with the same task requirements. The additional model sizes do not introduce datasets, domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Act-only, CoT, ReAct, Reflexion, ReAct + Reflexion and ToT-BFS remain in their respective comparisons. Table 6 applies the existing comparison set to additional model sizes.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds evaluations with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct as additional model configurations. The previously reported sampling, splits, metrics and generation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 examines performance across smaller and larger model configurations, extending the scale analysis beyond the retained fixed-generator assistant-size ablation. Existing component ablations, parameter sweeps and case studies remain; the multi-trial analysis moves from Appendix B.2 to Section 4.8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained multi-trial curves concern successive task attempts, rather than statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds scale-specific results, including GA-Rollback + Reflexion average success rates of 34.5% for 3B and 57.0% for 32B. Existing benchmark, ablation, GPT-4o, cost and sensitivity results are retained. These are additional outcomes, not improvements to previously reported same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The trajectory formalization, rollback mathematics, feedback-confidence equation and Webshop reward definition are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about preventing error propagation, the two supporting strategies, benchmark effectiveness and plug-and-play integration. Additional scale results support those existing claims.

C2.justification: Limitations adds the inability to undo actions in some real environments and recommends validation before irreversible actions. It removes the explicit untested-code/tool-use caveat and the task-decomposition suggestion. Appendix B.3 also interprets the new size results as supporting robustness and scalability.

D1.justification: The documented hardware, token limits, temperature, feedback threshold, Wait-Info and rollback settings, assistant prompts and code-access link are retained. No additional implementation or reproduction instructions accompany the new scale results.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the two Chen et al. translation references with Zhang et al. (2024) and Zuo et al. (2025), adds Tang et al. (2025) on role-playing agents, and removes ReGAL. The central positioning around LLM agents and self-correction remains.

P1.justification: The multi-trial analysis moves into Section 4.8, the Wait-Info and tree-search subsections exchange order, and Appendix B is reorganized. Local edits clarify the Webshop example, revise limitations, update author information and add acknowledgments; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 6 and moves Figure 6 into the main text. Figure 2 redraws the low-quality-feedback continuation path, and several plots and tables receive styling changes. The existing displays largely retain their content and the overall two-column layout.

improvement.justification: Table 6 provides useful additional evidence about performance at smaller and larger model scales, while the revised Limitations makes the practical requirement for reversible environments explicit. These are bounded improvements to empirical support and applicability guidance. Although the explicit untested-code/tool-use caveat is removed, the additions provide a modest net benefit; the method and principal results remain unchanged.
